frequency_question: How often do proposed joint resolutions of disapproval against nuclear cooperation agreements successfully pass both houses and survive/override an executive veto within the review window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements and major nuclear pacts submitted to Congress where a joint resolution of disapproval was introduced and brought to a vote. Excludes informal understandings not subject to formal statutory disapproval windows.

coverage_note: 3 named historical instances where statutory disapproval mechanisms were triggered for major nuclear agreements; none successfully blocked the agreement via a veto-proof joint resolution.
known_gaps: Minor non-nuclear international compacts reviewed under different statutes are excluded as they lack the specific high threshold of 123 agreements.
skeleton: Total formal congressional review cycles for major nuclear agreements where disapproval was seriously attempted vs. successful overrides.
multiplier: 0 successful veto-proof joint resolutions of disapproval out of historical major nuclear cooperation review cycles.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing 123 agreements remain stable under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 unless Congress amends the underlying statute.
